title: Commentaries of Proclus on the Timaeus, Vol. 1
author: Proclus (Taylor trans)
description: Commentaries of Proclus on the Timaeus of Plato, Volume 1, translated from the Greek by Thomas Taylor (London, 1820), in five books (the full work spans two volumes). Proclus's commentary on the Timaeus, the most important surviving ancient commentary on a Platonic dialogue, interprets Plato's cosmology in the light of the whole Neoplatonic theology. This volume covers the opening of the dialogue: the recapitulation of the Republic, the Atlantis story told by Critias and its allegorical meaning, and the beginning of Timaeus's discourse on the Demiurge, the paradigm, the generation of the cosmos and its being, drawing extensively on earlier commentators such as Porphyry and Iamblichus and on Orphic and Chaldean theology. Taylor's notes, typical of his advocacy for Platonism, supplement the text. It is indispensable for the history of Platonic cosmology and esoteric interpretation of the Timaeus.
